title: CLIO Wordle study technical walkthrough
audience: Technical viewers evaluating CLIO workflows, subagents, scientific provenance and interactive study views

audio.captions: Optional timestamped presenter draft with later ElevenLabs alignment import

takeaway: Follow a question into parallel experiments, inspect an agent making a move, and trace the resulting observation through review into an explorable study view.
sourceStrategy: Use the 60-game run for the complete flow and science-log investigation. Switch explicitly to the separate 30-game run for its attached study views. Preserve each run's identity, strategies, sample size, entries and results.

sources.liveWordleData: Recorded tool uiEvent messages: BoardWall component/spec, group, game key, rows and view

selectedGame.note: This worker interleaves five games and logs observations later. Do not move the observation to the instant of the final guess.

boards.dataMode: Static transcription of completed games, not a live feed of ongoing games

semantics: A flow is a procedure; this recording uses the workflow flow to execute a data-defined dependency graph, not a newly authored Python flow.
Ready independent steps may run in parallel. Merge waits for its three dependencies; the recorded final check/review follows merge.
The study log contains typed linked records. Status changes append records; they do not rewrite old evidence.
Science log List, Graph and Views are modes of one native tab. Views are dashboards attached by recorded view entries.
The log validates shapes and references; it does not establish scientific correctness. Recorded conflicts and caveats remain visible.
Editors and forks are capabilities, but neither supplied saved flow contains an added workflow step. Delegated game workers are not newly invented workflow steps.

visualGrammar.home: Native conversation at left and the native canvas at right; hide the workspace sidebar when it consumes reading space.
visualGrammar.rule: One principal canvas view at a time. Use real native navigation and restore the same source instant on a deliberate inspection pause.
visualGrammar.flowRevisits: Show the graph at launch, before opening a worker, after returning from the worker, and as merge/check become eligible.
visualGrammar.fullScreen: Use the native maximize/full-screen control only for a useful graph or board inspection, then restore it. No whole-window pseudozoom or duplicate plot crop.
visualGrammar.text: Public assistant prose is retyped uniformly within its recorded block boundaries. Weighted source-clock segments give burst-delivered sentences readable time and compress idle gaps. Original token checkpoints remain available for source inspection.
visualGrammar.pointer: One measured viewport pointer. Park until a distance-bounded 0.35-1 second approach; never interpolate the first move across the whole opening or return to a distant corner after each action.
labels: From a move to an observation
visualGrammar.runChange: Change the native session context and state once in narration that the views belong to a second, 10-seed-per-strategy run. For a silent cut, use one brief explicit transition caption.
visualGrammar.scrolling: Bake measured native transcript heights into the NDP damped viewport path. Reset between conversations. Short completed tool groups hold 100ms and collapse over 183ms; they do not inherit SPOTTER thinking holds.

chapters.title: A question CLIO can investigate
chapters.purpose: Establish the user task and the relevant agent without a long logo introduction.
actions: Open the native CLIO Science conversation with the Wordle tools carried by this recorded agent.
Type the actual user request; keep the tool-list restriction and agent-chosen guesses visible.
Let the first recorded public explanation arrive.
chapters.visibleEffect: The viewer sees a scientific study beginning from a normal request, not a prebuilt dashboard.
chapters.narration: The question is which strategy works on this tool's own word list. CLIO will test competing approaches and record the evidence.
chapters.clock: Recorded progression; brisk input, readable completed prompt.

chapters.title: Turn the request into a study
chapters.purpose: Make hypotheses and falsifiable predictions concrete.
actions: Show the relevant word-list inspection and log_entry tools in the normal chat flow.
Open workspace canvas, then Science log in Graph mode.
Show the question and three hypotheses arriving at their recorded times; select one and reveal its claim and refuting prediction.
chapters.visibleEffect: The log grows from an empty study into linked question/hypothesis records before results exist.
chapters.narration: These are competing hypotheses with explicit refuting predictions. The log keeps their identity as separate branches investigate them.
chapters.clock: Progress during entry arrival; one brief explicit inspection pause for the selected record.

chapters.title: Read the workflow before following it
chapters.purpose: Explain the real dependency graph and what parallel means here.
actions: Show the successful run_workflow call and its native flow card.
Open the workflow in the native side panel; use full screen briefly only if needed to read the graph.
Inspect the three strategy steps, merge and check. Show the three independent steps running while merge/check wait.
chapters.visibleEffect: The static dependency plan becomes a running workflow with three separate active branches.
chapters.narration: This run uses a workflow: a flow whose steps are data. The three experiments can run together; merge waits for all three, and the independent check follows merge.
chapters.clock: Shared recorded time; selected-step reading may use a declared global inspection pause.

chapters.title: Open a branch while it works
chapters.purpose: Connect a graph node to its actual worker and hypothesis.
actions: Select english while all strategy branches are still active.
Read the selected step's dependency/instruction summary, then use its native Open action.
Show the branch's recorded experiment and delegation call; expose the batch workers through their native task/session actions.
chapters.visibleEffect: The selected workflow step leads to a working conversation, not a separate explanatory scene.
chapters.narration: The node is an agent doing real work. This branch tests the English-style opener and splits its games among delegated workers.
chapters.clock: Navigation preserves the global source clock. Show existing worker history as history, then continue its current recorded stream.

chapters.title: Follow one worker and one game
chapters.purpose: Show tools visibly changing a real Wordle A2UI board.
actions: Open the recorded terva seeds 16-20 worker and its board presentation.
Follow game g36-s16: new-game call, a guess call, returned feedback and the corresponding tile update.
Show the three recorded guesses for that game with readable feedback. Keep interleaved games in their actual source order rather than pretending this worker only played one game.
chapters.visibleEffect: Letters and feedback change only when the matching recorded tool result arrives.
chapters.narration: The worker chooses the guesses. The tool supplies feedback; the Wordle board renders that returned state. These moves will become a measurement in the study.
chapters.clock: Continuous progression with idle-time compression; slow down for each shown guess/result/board transition. Other branches continue on the same clock.

chapters.title: Trace the game into the science log
chapters.purpose: Demonstrate provenance rather than merely displaying a result count.
actions: Condense the worker's remaining batch activity and reach the actual logging time for observation e_eabe97d01f4b.
Open that worker's Science log record; show guesses/solved measurements and seed/strategy conditions.
Expand Sources, then use View in transcript on one cited Wordle call and return to the observation.
chapters.visibleEffect: The displayed measurement is tied to the exact worker, game and returned tool data.
chapters.narration: This is one observation for a completed game, with its conditions and the recorded calls behind it. The source links take us back to the actual move.
chapters.clock: Do not backdate the observation to the final guess. Freeze all source projections during citation inspection, then resume together.

chapters.title: Return to the other experiments
chapters.purpose: Prove that background work continued during the active worker sequence.
actions: Return through native navigation to the workflow at the current source time.
Show the changed branch states and accumulated log entries.
Open a second strategy briefly, show its different opener and actual in-progress work, then return. Use the same seed only if its recorded state is available at this source time.
chapters.visibleEffect: The viewer sees concurrent work and meaningful differences between branches, without restarting their histories.
chapters.narration: While that worker played, the other branches kept running. They share the seed set, but investigate different strategies independently.
chapters.clock: Progress during navigation; no global hold added merely because one transcript paragraph is complete.

chapters.title: Watch the study record accumulate
chapters.purpose: Show the science log evolving over the run rather than appearing complete.
actions: Return to Science log List mode and expand the actual study/step/delegated-worker tree.
Show more observations arriving as workers complete their batches.
Select a branch to change Log of without leaving the current conversation; show a recorded evidence entry only after its analysis is available.
chapters.visibleEffect: The tree, per-branch log and accepted observation count develop from the same source events as the conversations.
chapters.narration: The study record is shared across branches. Observations, analysis and evidence retain their authors and links instead of becoming one flattened answer.
chapters.clock: Recorded progression with readable local selections. Apply canonical science.entry events, not every log_entry attempt.

chapters.title: Dependencies unlock merge and check
chapters.purpose: Complete the workflow story with real state transitions and independent checking.
actions: Return to the flow as the last strategy completes; let merge become active at its actual start.
Open the merge's analysis briefly and show a real evidence/conclusion link.
Show merge finishing, check starting, and the checker's actual recorded work before the workflow completes.
chapters.visibleEffect: A completed dependency unlocks the next stage, and the checker visibly does work before the green final graph appears.
chapters.narration: Merge starts only after the experiments finish. The final check is a separate recorded step, not a completion badge painted over the analysis.
chapters.clock: As-of task lifecycle and source text; never reveal final node statuses at launch.

chapters.title: Read the evidence behind the answer
chapters.purpose: Show how the science log supports inspection and preserves uncertainty.
actions: Switch the native Science log from List to Graph.
Select the recorded conclusion, use Selected and linked, and follow a cited evidence or conflict record.
Show Status reason or Sources on that selected record, then restore Entire study and return to the concise native answer.
chapters.visibleEffect: The conclusion's links lead back into the study; the recorded conflicts and sample-size limits remain visible.
chapters.narration: The log checks structure and references, not scientific truth. Here the study cannot reliably separate the openers, and its caveats remain connected to the answer.
chapters.clock: Deliberate review of the completed first run; source remains at its completed state.

chapters.title: A second recorded study adds views
chapters.purpose: Make the source change explicit before showing different strategies and numbers.
actions: Switch the native session context to the later Wordle study.
State that this is the separate ten-seed-per-strategy run, with 30 games.
Show the recorded view-creation/attachment activity and then open Science log Views; do not manufacture this action in the first run.
chapters.visibleEffect: The user understands why this chapter has different results and an English-style opener named anori.
chapters.narration: This second run uses ten seeds per strategy and attaches its own interactive views to the study.
chapters.clock: Explicit chapter cut between distinct source clocks; preserve order within the second run. Select its view-creation segment rather than replaying the whole experiment again.

chapters.title: Inspect the attached comparison view
chapters.purpose: Show a useful view reading the study's actual measurements.
actions: Open Guesses per game by strategy inside native Science log Views.
Use native maximize if needed for legibility and hover a specific seeded point to reveal its actual value and seed.
Show the native data/details action only if it exists and exposes the selected study rows; keep means 3.6, 4.2 and 4.0 associated with this run.
chapters.visibleEffect: The attached view exposes the measurements behind the summary without a separate rebuilt chart.
chapters.narration: This chart reads the study measurements. It compares the same seeds across strategies; the observed means are not a claim of a conclusive winner.
chapters.clock: Completed-study inspection. The comparison view was created after these games, so do not portray it as watching this recorded run grow live.

chapters.title: Change the seed and compare the boards
chapters.purpose: Make a control produce a clear, meaningful change in the displayed data.
actions: Switch the native study-view title selector to Game boards by seed; show seed 5's three boards.
Inspect B's six-guess game beside A's four-guess game; hover a relevant tile to show its recorded guess, feedback and observation ID.
Click seed 10 and show all three panels changing. Inspect the recorded inconsistent guess rather than adding arbitrary highlights.
Restore the native workspace before leaving the view.
chapters.visibleEffect: A real seed selection changes the three boards, and a tile tooltip identifies the logged source record.
chapters.narration: Seed five makes the different choices easy to see. Seed ten also exposes a protocol deviation. These boards are a saved reconstruction of the logged games, not a live game feed.
chapters.clock: Completed second-run review. Keep the editorial cursor live above native menus and tooltips.

chapters.title: Return from the view to its evidence
chapters.purpose: Close the provenance loop for the attached view.
actions: Return to the native Science log and select the observation or conflict relevant to the inspected game.
Use its native Sources or View in transcript action; do not invent a click-through on a tile whose saved specification only defines a tooltip.
Return to the study's conclusion with its low-confidence qualification visible.
chapters.visibleEffect: The visual inspection leads back to a recorded observation and its source rather than ending on an attractive but disconnected chart.
chapters.narration: The view helps us inspect a case. The study record preserves the calls and qualifications needed to judge it.
chapters.clock: Completed-study inspection; preserve native tab and scroll continuity.

chapters.title: Finish on the inspectable study
chapters.purpose: Leave the product outcome clear without a long static outro.
actions: Hold the readable final workspace briefly with the conclusion and an attached view.
Use a short CLIO closing only if it does not displace the result.
chapters.visibleEffect: A question has become parallel work, recorded evidence and views the user can inspect.
chapters.narration: The outcome is an experiment you can follow and inspect, including where its evidence is still uncertain.
chapters.clock: Completed state; no fabricated further work.

replayContract: Use one source clock per recorded run. Route every visible session, task state, accepted science entry, Wordle update and table projection through it.
Parse all nested sessions and deduplicate semantic events by stable identity. The coordinator and delegated workers hold necessary events; root-only parsing is insufficient.
Join tool records to tool.call.started/completed via event_ids. Tool-record dictionaries alone contain no authoritative started_at/completed_at fields in these exports.

Hydrate workflow checkpoint content by its recorded descriptor when available; a checkpoint reference is not itself a renderable historical snapshot. Use recorded lifecycle observations and final flow handle mappings for supported projections, never arbitrary status animation.
Apply append-only science.entry records and status events by occurred_at. Rejected or retried tool invocations must not create extra observations or overwrite history.
Replay Wordle uiEvent updates by catalog, group and game key after their producing result. Do not treat this path as the same thing as an ordinary saved A2UI surface.
Keep source time advancing while browsing active workers unless the user-facing sequence deliberately enters an inspection pause. A completed paragraph in one pane must not freeze every other branch.
Open a worker at the current source instant, including existing history; do not retype its earlier work from frame zero. Returning to the flow shows its then-current state.

An inspection pause freezes every source projection, then all resume from the same instant. Cursor motion and native spinner animation use editorial frame time, not progress invented for the underlying work.
Preload data and native components, but reveal records and results only after their recorded arrival. No final-state leakage through prefetched graph nodes, statuses, boards or data tables.

Do not show the later study's generated views before their recorded attachment. Its CSV board view is a static post-study transcription; its comparison view's live-data capability does not mean a live-growing chart was recorded here.

excludeFromThisCut: A tour of every SDK/plugin or code-authoring a Python flow not present in these recordings
An invented editor-added step, fork, approval prompt, restart recovery or experiment extension
A universal best-Wordle-strategy claim from small agent-played samples
Unnecessary full-screen views, arbitrary text selections, mouse gestures without a meaningful data or navigation effect
A dashboard that appears to update before it was created, or a final-state graph used as the entire replay
Production notes, verbose provenance captions and long held introduction/outro cards
scienceLogDirection: Graph is the main view. Select nodes for their records and citations; use the task tree briefly for delegated-worker navigation.
revisionNotes: The 9:20 v1 was rejected for its dotted title, choppy text/scrolling, short-tool pauses and crawling first Science Log pointer.
The revised full timeline is 8:30. Source archives, event order, run boundaries and scientific qualifications are preserved.
Both the revised opening and full cut are encoded. Playback review is recorded separately from automated validation; creative acceptance remains with the user.
